answer: Copying the same citations across 252 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 252 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the anchor index resolves every citation against the voyage checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the nebula audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4939 identities would post 4916 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
